description:
Redwood Inference is expanding its Unified Rollouts/A-B testing and model lifecycle tooling. Today, model/version information is spread across the model registry, runtime config, and docs/release processes, which leads to inconsistent customer-facing change visibility (what changed, why it changed, how risky it is, and how to roll back). This project standardizes a single model/version metadata schema and builds an automated changelog generator that produces customer-visible release notes (Console + docs), while also supporting internal auditability and safe rollout policies.

Goals:
- Define and adopt a v1 metadata schema for all served models/variants/quantization profiles, including: semantic versioning, compatibility constraints, tokenizer/runtime requirements, safety/quality notes, deprecations, rollout eligibility, and per-deployment availability (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).
- Generate customer-visible release notes automatically from model metadata + change events, with consistent language and categorization (security, breaking, perf, quality, bugfix, deprecation), and links to relevant guidance.
- Provide internal changelog/audit events for supportability (who changed what, when, where), and align with change-management expectations for enterprise/Private customers.

Scope (in):
- Schema definition (JSON Schema/Protobuf-style) + validation tooling.
- Storage and API surfaces in the control plane/model registry; migration of existing model records.
- Eventing for “model metadata changed” and “model version promoted” events; changelog generation pipeline.
- Console integration for release notes and per-model change history.
- Docs-site generation support (public release notes pages) and editorial guidelines.
- Evals/quality hooks: attach quality signals and guardrail outcomes to release notes (where appropriate).

Scope (out / later):
- Full customer notification subscriptions (email/webhook) beyond basic internal webhook plumbing.
- Rewriting all historical release notes; focus on forward-looking generation with a small backfill.

Primary stakeholders:
- Product: Marissa Cole (Dir PM Console & Rollouts), Paula Mendes (SPM)
- Engineering: Dylan Brooks (Dir Eng Console & Tooling), Chloe Martin (EM Console Backend), Ethan Park (EM Control Plane)
- Key ICs: Jada Williams (Staff Console), Quentin Harris (Model Catalog), Michael Nguyen (Control Plane), Connor O'Brien (Release Eng)
- Partners: Jonas Weber / Sana Farid (Evals/metrics), DevEx/Docs team, Security & Compliance for audit logging expectations, Support/CS for customer escalations.

Timeline (illustrative, ~10–12 weeks):
1) Discovery + design (2–3 wks): inventory existing metadata, draft schema, align on source-of-truth and publishing rules; write ADRs and PRD; early design mocks.
2) Implementation (4–5 wks): model registry schema + migrations; API endpoints; validation in CI; changelog generator service/library; PR labeling conventions.
3) Integration + QA (2–3 wks): Console UI integration, docs-site build integration, end-to-end tests, Private packaging considerations.
4) Rollout + GA (1–2 wks): dogfood internally, limited beta on 1–2 enterprise accounts, publish guidelines, measure support ticket reduction and release-note coverage.

Key deliverables:
- Model metadata schema v1 (with validation rules and examples)
- Changelog generator and templates
- Console and docs integration
- Change/audit event documentation
- Operational runbooks for publishing/rollback and support workflows

Constraints and risks:
- Must avoid leaking sensitive/internal-only details in customer-visible notes; needs a clear “public vs internal” field strategy.
- Backward compatibility for pinned model versions and Private offline bundles.
- Statistical rigor for A/B quality claims; release notes must not overstate.
- Multi-deployment consistency: Hosted, Dedicated, and Private may differ in availability/rollout timing.

files.description: PRD: problem statement, user stories (customers/support/release eng), success metrics, non-goals, MVP definition, and phased rollout plan for schema + changelog generator.
Design spec for Console surfaces: per-model change history, filtering by deployment/region, and how release notes appear during rollouts (canary/A-B).
Editorial rules for customer-visible notes: categories, severity language, breaking-change rules, examples, and redaction guidelines.
Formal schema v1 definition: required/optional fields, invariants, compatibility semantics, versioning rules, and example payloads for common model families.
ADR deciding the source of truth (model registry vs control plane), publishing workflow, and how public/internal fields are handled.
ADR comparing approaches: changelog from registry events, from GitHub PR labels, or hybrid; final decision and trade-offs.
System doc: service responsibilities, data flow, APIs, event schema, storage, and failure modes for the changelog generator.
CI/CD standard: how metadata changes are validated, how release note artifacts are built, and required checks before promotion.
Docs playbook: how docs builds consume generated notes, routing/URLs, and how to handle embargoed or customer-specific changes.
Security/compliance doc: audit event types for model/version metadata changes, retention expectations, and SIEM export considerations.
Private deployments guidance: how release notes map to upgrade bundles, offline environments, and rollback documentation requirements.
Working PRD outline with open questions, stakeholder notes, and early MVP scoping; includes links to Linear tickets and early customer feedback.
Engineering draft: options for generator (library vs service), templating approach, backfill strategy, and API contract sketches.
Spreadsheet-style doc: inventory of existing model records, required field backfill, risk classification, and migration checklist by deployment mode.
Working notes defining PR labels/fields required to generate consistent notes; examples of good/bad release-note entries.
Brainstorm: which eval metrics can be safely summarized in release notes, and what qualifies as a meaningful quality change.
QA/test plan draft: end-to-end scenarios (metadata edit, version promotion, rollback), and how to validate public/internal separation.
CS draft FAQ: how customers interpret model version changes, what’s included in notes, and troubleshooting guidance for regressions.
Parent PM ticket: MVP definition, milestones, launch criteria, and coordination tasks across Eng/Docs/CS/Security.
Eng ticket: implement schema definition + validation tooling; includes examples and required fields for launch.
Eng ticket: DB/storage migration plan, backfill, and rollout sequencing; includes risk mitigation and rollback plan.
Eng ticket: implement generator (event ingestion + templating) and provide internal APIs for Console/docs builds.
Eng ticket: Console backend endpoints + pagination/filtering; ties to design spec and RBAC requirements.
Eng/Security joint ticket: define and enforce redaction rules; includes review checklist and test cases.
Eng/Release ticket: add CI checks to validate schema diffs and produce preview release-note artifacts for reviewer approval.
Eng/Applied ML ticket: attach eval run IDs, baseline comparisons, and guardrail outcomes to model version metadata.
Eng/Security ticket: emit audit events for create/update/promote/deprecate actions; ensure coverage in Private deployments.
Design ticket: wireframes and interaction details for viewing release notes during rollouts and browsing model history.
Eng ticket: export release notes with Private upgrade artifacts; includes offline packaging constraints.
PM ticket: beta customer criteria, comms plan, success metrics, and coordination with CS/support readiness.
PR: introduces schema v1, adds JSON Schema validation in CI, and includes example fixtures for common model families and quantization profiles.
PR: database migration + backfill job; includes rollback steps, safety checks, and metrics to monitor migration health.
PR: emits structured events on model metadata changes and version promotions; includes event schema and idempotency logic.
PR: adds changelog generator library/service with templating, category mapping, and public/internal field filtering.
PR: adds Console backend APIs for release notes feed and per-model change history; includes pagination, filtering, and RBAC checks.
PR: CI job that produces a release note preview artifact for review; fails builds when required fields or redaction rules are violated.
PR: emits audit log events for model changes and exposes internal admin query endpoints used by support and compliance.
PR: hotfix ensuring internal-only release note fields never render for standard roles; includes regression test.
PR: docs build step consumes generated changelog artifacts and renders versioned release note pages and RSS/JSON feed.
PR: publishes style guide content and examples; documents what constitutes breaking vs non-breaking model changes.
PR: SDK support for querying model metadata and release notes; adds typed response models and pagination helpers.
PR: TypeScript SDK adds metadata types, fetchers, and examples for consuming release notes programmatically.
PR: ensures eval runs record model version + metadata schema hash; enables traceability from release notes to eval evidence.
PR: adds dashboards/metrics correlating incidents or regressions with model version change events and rollout phases.
